To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the rotation curve of a thin disc of self-gravitating matter is exactly flat in the absence of any extended halo or modified gravity; 2) the disc density can be inferred from the rotation curve; 3) the density is always "exponential" in the sense of having a Gaussian profile in the logarithm of the radius; and 4) a disc can contain the majority (90-99%) of its total mass in a vast mass "hinderland",

thin discs of self-gravitating matter alone can support flat rotation curves, that the density of such discs can be inferred from their rotation curves, and that the discs possess vast outer mass hinterlands that can contain most of their mass.
